exitCriteria.title: The scheduled job runs exactly four times daily in both halves of the year, verified across a daylight saving transition
exitCriteria.reason: The gate now decides from the cron slot GitHub reports rather than the wall clock at gate time, so a run queued hours late is still judged by the slot it was scheduled for, and the eight UTC entries open exactly the four required America/Vancouver hours in both halves of the year. That closes a measured defect: across the 100 most recent scheduled runs the wall-clock gate opened 39 where the design intends 50, and zero or one a day through the week to 2026-09-02. Two things still keep this criterion failing. GitHub created only four of the eight scheduled runs a day over that same week, so the cadence depends on a scheduler that promises nothing and can only be shown by observation over a real window, including one that crosses a daylight saving transition. And real refreshes have been observed only over a short window: on the merge commit of #165 the gate opened three of the six scheduled runs GitHub created between 2026-09-13 and 2026-09-14, and each of those three fetched all four owner-admitted feeds, archived them under a two-year COMPLIANCE lock that read back, and published a status version. GitHub created no run for the 12:17 or 13:17 UTC slots on 2026-09-14 by the time the runs were read, and no observed run crosses a daylight saving transition. Code that decides correctly is not evidence that a scheduled run has succeeded.

exitCriteria.title: Both public routes retain the five required safety display fields and block deployment if one is absent
exitCriteria.reason: Rendered route tests require source updated, last successful refresh, source agency, next scheduled refresh, and official emergency information in both English and French; deleting a field fails the validator. On 2026-09-23 wildfire-routes.test.tsx changed for a plain-language wording pass alone; its digest was refreshed, and this reason still holds.

exitCriteria.title: At 25 hours without a successful refresh, the static route shows unavailable guidance and an agency link
exitCriteria.reason: The stale-state contract begins after 24 hours, removes the derived illustrative summary, and retains official-agency guidance. The workflow test covers the stricter 25-hour case through the same persisted last-success state. On 2026-09-23 wildfire-routes.test.tsx changed for a plain-language wording pass alone; its digest was refreshed, and this reason still holds.

exitCriteria.title: A full simulated season of immutable snapshots is retained and queryable by bounded time range
exitCriteria.reason: The local store writes each raw snapshot with exclusive create, never queries current.json as history, and the simulated May–September season test retains 612 snapshots then queries a bounded July interval.

productionBlockers.reason: No production route may use the fixture or any configured endpoint until every feed has a documented authoritative endpoint, rights, version/snapshot contract, archive admission, and production approval. SOPFEU remains rights-and-snapshot-blocked.
There is no observed production scheduler/storage/monitoring/on-call rehearsal for outage, schema change, stale state, and daylight-saving transitions. Local simulation is not operational evidence.

safetyBoundary: This local contract provides context only: it is not emergency direction, a spread prediction, or a damage map.
